answer_text: OAuth access tokens are credentials used to access protected resources; they represent authorization issued to a client and can replace other authorization constructs with a single token understood by the resource server. A JWT MUST NOT be accepted for processing on or after its 'exp' (expiration) time; the current date/time must be before the expiration date/time, with a possible small leeway for clock skew.
A resource owner in OAuth 2.0 is an entity capable of granting access to a protected resource. When the resource owner is a person, it is referred to as an end-user.
In OAuth 2.0, the resource server is the role that hosts protected resources and accepts access tokens.
The OAuth role that hosts protected resources and accepts access tokens is the resource server. [Kb117ef7af6e7058a]

OAuth refresh tokens must not be sent to resource servers; they are only shared with the authorization server.
